The largest country in the world is Russia.

To understand the concept of relativity described in your text, imagine time as a river flowing at a steady pace for everyone. In our everyday lives, this river flows at the same speed for you, me, and the person standing next to us. However, Einstein’s theory of relativity suggests that this "river" can actually speed up or slow down depending on how fast you are moving or how strong the gravity is around you.

Think of it like a rubber band. If you pull the rubber band tight (which represents moving very fast, close to the speed of light, or being in a strong gravitational field), the band stretches. In this analogy, the stretching represents time slowing down. So, if you are on that train moving incredibly fast, you are like someone holding one end of the stretched rubber band. To you, the seconds tick by normally because you are moving *with* the stretched time. But to an observer standing still on the platform, they see your rubber band stretched out, meaning your seconds are taking much longer to pass compared to theirs. This is why your clock appears to tick slower to the outside observer, even though you feel like time is passing normally for you.
